minutes.headline: Commission ordered the Baloney greenhouse moved out of the wetland buffer; it approved retaining-wall and delineation filings.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission opened with a hearing on an enforcement matter at 23 Cope, where a 10x10 greenhouse sits within the wetland buffer, and voted to require its relocation. It then approved a retaining wall NOI at 42 Pearl Street, an ANRAD at 400 Leominster-Shirley Road, three Lake Shirley retaining wall NOIs on Round Road, and two certificates of compliance. The chair also discussed possible grant projects for conservation land trails and parking.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted to require relocation of a greenhouse at 23 Cope that sits within the wetland buffer; the roll call was 4 to 1 as heard.
The applicants will work with the administrator on a schedule to relocate or remove the greenhouse, and she will update the commission.
The commission approved a retaining-wall filing at 42 Pearl Street and a wetland boundary determination at 400 Leominster Shirley Road.
It approved three Lake Shirley retaining-wall filings on Round Road, each with pre-construction meeting and construction schedule conditions.
The commission approved two certificates of compliance on Cross Road, and the chair and one member will pursue conservation grants due at the end of January.

why_it_matters: Owners with structures inside a wetland buffer can be ordered to move them, and neighbors citing past exceptions did not change the outcome here.
Lakefront owners planning retaining walls on Lake Shirley face approval conditions, and the commission's conservation land trail and parking grants may bring cash matches from the Timber rights fund.
watch_next: The administrator's update on the greenhouse relocation schedule and her review of old enforcement orders before the next meeting.
The amount of the increase to the kiosk materials purchase order, deferred to the next meeting, and the grant applications due at the end of January.
